summary: Describes a URN namespace for identifying NewsML news items. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: News stories need permanent name tags so they can always be found. This defines the name format for one news file type.

questions: how to name news items with urns
subtitle: A permanent naming scheme for news items in NewsML format

tldr.problem: News items need a permanent, unique name that persists even if the item moves to a different location on the web. NewsML is an XML format for news, but items need stable URN identifiers independent of URLs.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC defines a URN namespace called 'newsml' with a structure of ProviderId, DateId, NewsItemId, RevisionId and an optional Update flag, allowing news providers to allocate unique names to their items.
tldr.outcome: News providers can now assign and track versions of news items with persistent identifiers that survive relocation, though the actual adoption depends on the newsml ecosystem.

today: RFC 3085 is an Informational RFC defining the newsml URN namespace and has not been obsoleted. It remains the specification for how news providers allocate URNs to NewsML items.

sections.title: NewsML and URN Naming
sections.content:
NewsML is an XML format for packaging multimedia news resources. It was created under the auspices of the International Press Telecommunications Council (IPTC). The RFC defines a URN (Uniform Resource Name) namespace for identifying NewsML NewsItems—individual information resources expressible as NewsML elements within a NewsML document conforming to the NewsML Document Type Declaration.

The same logical NewsItem may exist in multiple physical locations. While NewsML allows NewsItems to have multiple URLs, a single URN provides the unique, persistent identifier. The namespace is intended as a formal namespace following RFC 2611 requirements.
sections.plainLanguage: News files can move around the web, but they need one permanent name that never changes. This RFC explains how to name each news story so it can always be found.

sections.title: URN Structure and Components
sections.content:
The NewsML URN namespace is requested as 'newsml'. The URN identifier follows this ABNF structure:

NSS = ProviderId ":" DateId ":" NewsItemId ":" RevisionId Update

The ProviderId must be an Internet domain name owned by the organisation creating the NewsML resource. The DateId is a date in ISO 8601 Basic Format (CCYYMMDD) indicating when the organisation owned that domain name. The NewsItemId must be unique among all NewsItems from the same provider with the same DateId. The RevisionId is a positive integer (never zero) indicating which revision of a NewsItem this is; larger values indicate more recent revisions. The optional Update flag is 'U' if the NewsItem contains Update elements or 'A' if it contains only replacement NewsManagement data; if neither, it is omitted.
sections.plainLanguage: The news name has four parts: who wrote it (domain name), when they owned that domain (date), what news it is (ID number), and which version of the story (revision number). An extra flag says if this is an update or replacement.

sections.title: Uniqueness and Persistence
sections.content:
The combination of ProviderId and DateId uniquely identifies the organisation allocating the URN. That organisation is responsible for ensuring uniqueness of the DateId/NewsItemId/RevisionId combination. Since a NewsML URN may only be allocated by an organisation that owns an Internet domain name, the URN identifies a date on which the organisation owned that domain name. This combination of date and domain name uniquely identifies that organisation for all time, ensuring identifier persistence.

News providers are responsible for providing URN resolution services if any for URNs they have assigned. URNs are lexically equivalent if the ProviderId, DateId, NewsItemId and RevisionId are all identical using case-insensitive comparison. Organisations may also provide validation services for URNs with a valid ProviderId/DateId combination.
sections.plainLanguage: No two news stories can have the same name because the domain name plus date plus story number plus version creates billions of possible combinations. The news provider keeps track of which names they gave out.

sections.title: Example URNs
sections.content:
Example NewsML URNs include:

urn:newsml:iptc.org:20001006:NewsMLv1.0:1

urn:newsml:reuters.com:20000206:IIMFFH05643_2000-02-06_17-54-01_L06156584:1U

The first example uses IPTC's domain (iptc.org) with date 6 October 2000, a NewsItemId of 'NewsMLv1.0', and revision 1 with no Update flag. The second uses Reuters' domain (reuters.com) with date 6 February 2000, a longer alphanumeric NewsItemId, revision 1, and the 'U' flag indicating it contains Updates.
sections.plainLanguage: Here are two real examples of what these permanent news names look like: one from IPTC, one from Reuters. Each one uniquely identifies one version of a specific news story from a specific company on a specific date.

sections.title: Security and Scope
sections.content:
There are no additional security considerations beyond those normally associated with the use and resolution of URNs in general. The scope of the newsml URN namespace is global, allowing any news provider with a registered domain name to participate.

The registration information notes that the namespace registration version is 1, with registration date 6 November 2000, and the declared registrant is David Allen of IPTC.
sections.plainLanguage: The naming scheme itself is not a security feature; it is just a permanent way to label news stories. Normal web security rules apply when finding or using the news items.
